questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Solve the expression by grouping **Addition** and **Subtraction** terms after basic operations. Identify values: 92 − 56 + 78 − (48) + 54. Sum of positive terms: 92 + 78 + 54 = 224. Sum of negative terms: 56 + 48 = 104. Final calculation: 224 − 104 = 120. **∴ The correct answer is 120.**

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply **VBODMAS**: Bracket → Division → Multiplication → Addition → Subtraction.

74 + 38 − 19 + 47 − 16 + 25

Group positive and negative terms: (74 + 38 + 47 + 25) − (19 + 16)

184 − 35 = 149

**∴ The correct answer is 149.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** 74 + (19 × 2) − 38 ÷ 2 + 47 − 16 + 25

Solving following the **BODMAS** rule:

⇒ 74 + 38 − 38 ÷ 2 + 47 − 16 + 25 (Solving bracket: 19 × 2 = 38)

⇒ 74 + 38 − 19 + 47 − 16 + 25 (Solving division: 38 ÷ 2 = 19)

⇒ 112 − 19 + 47 − 16 + 25 (Adding 74 + 38 = 112)

⇒ 93 + 47 − 16 + 25 (Subtracting 112 − 19 = 93)

⇒ 140 − 16 + 25 (Adding 93 + 47 = 140)

⇒ 124 + 25 (Subtracting 140 − 16 = 124)

⇒ 149 (Final addition)

**∴ The correct answer is 149.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It specifies the order of operations: **Brackets**, **Orders** (powers/roots), **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**.

VBODMAS

The **V** stands for **Vinculum** (a bar over numbers), which has the highest priority even before the circular brackets.

Priority of Brackets

When multiple brackets are present, solve them in the order: **Parentheses ( )** → **Braces { }** → **Square Brackets [ ]**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Expand the decimals to compare digits: 0.1212..., 0.1717..., 0.2111..., 0.1919...

Compare the **tenths place** (first digit after the decimal).

The digits are 1, 1, 2, and 1 respectively.

Since 2 is the **largest digit**, 0.2111... must be the largest value.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.211... (recurring decimal).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Four recurring decimals to compare.

**Formula:** Convert recurring decimals into fractions to compare their magnitudes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a6bc92baa5fba2589a91b41f8c1c5df41e3907fb1d501e145fdceff1b2532307.png] 

⇒ 0.1212... = 12/99

⇒ 0.1717... = 17/99

⇒ 0.2111... = (21 − 2)/90 = 19/90

⇒ 0.1919... = 19/99

⇒ Comparing 19/90 and 19/99: Since the **numerator** is the same, the fraction with the **smaller denominator** is larger.

⇒ 19/90 > 19/99

⇒ Also, 19/99 is clearly larger than 17/99 and 12/99.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.211... (recurring decimal).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pure Recurring Decimals

A decimal where all digits after the point repeat, e.g., 0.ab... = ab/99.

Mixed Recurring Decimals

A decimal where some digits do not repeat, e.g., 0.abc... (bc repeating) = (abc − a)/990.

Comparison Rule

To compare decimals, align the decimal points and compare digits from left to right (tenths, then hundredths, etc.).

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Identify the **factors** of the denominators: (1×3), (3×5), (5×7), (7×9), (9×11), (11×13). The total **number of terms** (n) in this series is 6. Use the formula: **Sum = n / (First factor × Last factor)**. Here, First factor = 1 and Last factor = 13. Sum = 6 / (1 × 13) = 6/13. **∴ The correct answer is 6/13.**

questions.question: (54.87)² - (18.13)² = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Difference of Squares** formula: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).

Here, a = 54.87 and b = 18.13.

Sum (a + b) = 54.87 + 18.13 = 73.

Difference (a − b) = 54.87 − 18.13 = 36.74.

Result = 73 × 36.74 = 2682.02.

**∴ The correct answer is 2682.02.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = (54.87)² − (18.13)²

**Formula Used:**

Algebraic Identity: **a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)**

**Calculations:**

⇒ (54.87 + 18.13) × (54.87 − 18.13)

⇒ 73 × 36.74

⇒ 73 × (36 + 0.74)

⇒ (73 × 36) + (73 × 0.74)

⇒ 2628 + 54.02

⇒ 2682.02

**∴ The correct answer is 2682.02.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference of Squares Identity

The identity **a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)** is highly effective for simplifying calculations involving squares of decimal numbers or large integers.

Square of a Sum

The formula **(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²** is used to find the square of a number by breaking it into a sum of two easier numbers.

Square of a Difference

The formula **(a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²** is used when it is easier to express a number as a difference (e.g., 99 = 100 − 1).

questions.question: The adjacent angles of a parallelogram are in the ratio of 2 : 3. What are the measure (in degrees) of the larger angle?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ In a **parallelogram**, the sum of **adjacent angles** is always 180°. Ratio of angles = 2 : 3 Total units = 2 + 3 = 5 units 5 units = 180° ⇒ 1 unit = 36° **Larger angle** = 3 units = 3 × 36° = 108°. **∴ The correct answer is 108°.**

questions.question: What is the smallest number that is a multiple of 7, 10, 14 and 20?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **smallest number** that is a multiple of 7, 10, 14, and 20, identify the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)**.

Pick the **largest number** (20) and check its multiples: 20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, 140...

Check **divisibility** for each: 140 is the first multiple divisible by both **7** and **14**.

Since 140 is also divisible by 10, it is the **smallest common multiple**.

**∴ The correct answer is 140.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers are 7, 10, 14, and 20.

**Formula Used:** **LCM** = Product of the **highest powers** of all prime factors involved.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5c704fe1faf00eb164a75fe2a93578e7ac3232cb6cc19019801a4cfe5f7ae0ae.png] 

⇒ **Prime factorization** of numbers:

⇒ 7 = 7¹

⇒ 10 = 2¹ × 5¹

⇒ 14 = 2¹ × 7¹

⇒ 20 = 2² × 5¹

⇒ LCM = 2² × 5¹ × 7¹

⇒ LCM = 4 × 5 × 7 = 140

**∴ The correct answer is 140.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The **LCM** of a set of numbers is the smallest integer that is exactly divisible by every number in that set.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The **HCF** is the greatest number that divides two or more numbers without leaving a remainder.

Fundamental Property of LCM and HCF

For any two numbers **a** and **b**, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their **HCF** and **LCM** (a × b = HCF × LCM).

questions.question: 3 different pieces of iron with lengths 81 cm, 54 cm and 36 cm. Rods are to be made by cutting these pieces. Each rod should be of same length. No iron is to be wasted. What is the length (in cm) of longest such rod?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ To find the length of the **longest rod** that divides multiple pieces without waste, calculate the **Highest Common Factor (HCF)**. HCF of (81, 54, 36) Difference between 81 and 54 = 27 Difference between 54 and 36 = 18 HCF of differences (27, 18) = 9 **∴ The correct answer is 9 cm.**

questions.question: When 10 percent of a number is added to 15 percent of the same number, then the result is 3375. What is the value of the number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Combine the **percentages** directly since they apply to the same **number**: 10% + 15% = 25%.

As per the given condition, 25% of the **number** → 3375.

We know that 25% is equivalent to the **fraction** 1/4.

Total **number** (100%) = 3375 × 4 = 13500.

**∴ The correct answer is 13500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of 10% and 15% of a **number** is 3375.

**Formula Used:** Value = (Percentage ÷ 100) × **Original Number**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8c406197e98fa6c6d7f9a819befe07ddcbe5c9fc8b4381e614e0f175ec49dfd0.png] 

⇒ Let the **number** be x.

⇒ 10% of x + 15% of x = 3375

⇒ (10 ÷ 100) × x + (15 ÷ 100) × x = 3375

⇒ 0.10x + 0.15x = 3375

⇒ 0.25x = 3375

⇒ x = 3375 ÷ 0.25

⇒ x = (3375 × 100) ÷ 25

⇒ x = 3375 × 4

⇒ x = 13500

**∴ The correct answer is 13500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Addition Rule

If multiple **percentages** are calculated on the same **base value**, they can be added or subtracted directly before performing the multiplication: a% of x + b% of x = (a + b)% of x.

Common Fraction Conversions

Converting percentages to **fractions** simplifies calculations: 25% = 1/4, 20% = 1/5, 10% = 1/10, and 50% = 1/2.

Finding the Original Value

To find the 100% value (the **number** itself) when a certain percentage P% is known as value V: Original Number = (V ÷ P) × 100.

questions.question: Selling price of an article is Rs. 510. Loss percentage is 15 percent. What is the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **Loss percentage** to fraction: 15% = 3/20.

If **Cost Price (CP)** = 20 units, then **Loss** = 3 units.

**Selling Price (SP)** = CP − Loss = 20 − 3 = 17 units.

Given 17 units = **₹510** ⇒ 1 unit = 510 ÷ 17 = **₹30**.

**Cost Price** = 20 units = 20 × 30 = **₹600**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Selling price** (SP) = ₹510

**Loss percentage** (L%) = 15%

**Formula Used:**

**Cost Price** (CP) = [100 ÷ (100 − L%)] × SP

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/881b4287e76076f547ddf7486cba28270725be1a669b2fa7857b62c1adcdee09.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = [100 ÷ (100 − 15)] × 510

⇒ CP = [100 ÷ 85] × 510

⇒ CP = [20 ÷ 17] × 510

⇒ CP = 20 × 30

⇒ CP = ₹600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100, where Profit = SP − CP. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100, where Loss = CP − SP.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always offered on the **Marked Price (MP)**. SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Successive Discounts

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the effective single discount is (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: A person sells an article at the profit of 10 percent. Cost price and selling price both are increased by 20 percent. What will be the new profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the **Cost Price (CP)** and **Selling Price (SP)** are both changed by the **same percentage**, the **Profit Percentage** remains **unchanged**.

Since both CP and SP are increased by 20%, their **ratio** (SP ÷ CP) remains the same.

Original Profit = 10% → New Profit = 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

questions.question: Weight of A and B are in the ratio of 6 : 5. B's weight increases by 20 percent. Total weight of A and B increases by 40 percent. If total weight of them becomes 154 kg, then what is the weight of A after the increment?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Initial Weights** be 60 kg and 50 kg (Ratio 6 : 5) ⇒ **Total Initial Weight** = 110 kg.

**New Total Weight** (40% increase) = 110 × 1.4 = 154 kg. (Matches given data).

**New Weight of B** (20% increase) = 50 × 1.2 = 60 kg.

**Weight of A after increment** = **New Total** − **New B** = 154 − 60 = 94 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 94 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Ratio of weights of A and B** = 6 : 5

**Increase in B** = 20%

**Increase in Total Weight** = 40%

**Final Total Weight** = 154 kg

**Formula Used:**

**Final Value** = **Initial Value** × (1 + **Percentage Increase** ÷ 100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/911a4b831015331ca6f10405b16c820aac1ff2628db560fb646f665cdc2332b4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Initial Total Weight** = 154 ÷ 1.4 = 110 kg

⇒ **Sum of Ratio Parts** = 6 + 5 = 11 units

⇒ **Initial Weight of A** = (6 ÷ 11) × 110 = 60 kg

⇒ **Initial Weight of B** = (5 ÷ 11) × 110 = 50 kg

⇒ **Weight of B after 20% increase** = 50 + (20% of 50) = 50 + 10 = 60 kg

⇒ **Weight of A after increment** = **New Total Weight** − **New Weight of B**

⇒ **Weight of A after increment** = 154 − 60 = 94 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 94 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average in Percentages

The net percentage change of a sum is the weighted average of the percentage changes of its components: Net % = (n₁ × p₁ + n₂ × p₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Ratio and Proportionality

When quantities are in a ratio a : b, their actual values can be represented as ax and bx, where x is the common multiplier found by dividing the total value by (a + b).

Percentage Multiplier Method

To increase a value by x%, multiply the original value by (1 + x/100). To decrease, multiply by (1 − x/100).

questions.question: A pipe can fill 5/6 part of a tank in 60 minutes. What part of the same tank it can fill in 30 minutes?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **part filled** is **directly proportional** to the **time** elapsed when the **filling rate** is constant.

Given: **60 minutes** → **5/6 part**

Since **30 minutes** is exactly **half** of 60 minutes, the part filled will also be **half**.

New Part = (5/6) × (30/60) = (5/6) × (1/2) = 5/12.

**∴ The correct answer is 5/12 part.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Part of tank filled (P₁) = 5/6

Time taken (T₁) = 60 min

Target Time (T₂) = 30 min

**Formula Used:**

**Rate** of filling = **Part filled** ÷ **Time taken**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3daaa31f080a78c9cd3b27ec57878c0c9d60d1aaf4160fa7519c11d343261184.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Rate of filling = (5/6) ÷ 60

⇒ Rate = 5 / (6 × 60) = 5/360 = 1/72 part per minute

⇒ Part filled in 30 minutes = Rate × Time

⇒ Part filled = (1/72) × 30

⇒ Part filled = 30/72

⇒ Dividing numerator and denominator by 6:

⇒ Part filled = 5/12

**∴ The correct answer is 5/12 part.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Variation

In filling problems, the **quantity** (part of the tank) is **directly proportional** to **time** (Q ∝ T), provided the rate of the pipe remains constant.

Filling Rate Formula

If a pipe fills a tank in **'x' minutes**, its filling rate is **1/x part** of the tank per minute.

Combined Pipes Rule

If pipe A fills a tank in **'a'** time and pipe B fills it in **'b'** time, together they fill **(1/a + 1/b) part** in unit time.

questions.question: A train of length 300 metres crosses a another train of length 500 metres in 90 seconds. They are travelling in opposite directions. If the speed of both the trains is same, then what is the speed (in km/hr) of each train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance to cover = Sum of **train lengths** = 300 + 500 = 800 m.

In **opposite directions**, relative speed = S₁ + S₂ = 2 × Speed (as speeds are same).

Relative Speed = Distance ÷ Time = 800 ÷ 90 = 80/9 m/s.

Speed of each train = (1/2) × (80/9) × (18/5) km/hr = 16 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Length of first train (L₁) = 300 m, Length of second train (L₂) = 500 m, **Time** (T) = 90 sec, Speed of both trains is equal (v).

**Formula:** Relative Speed = (L₁ + L₂) ÷ T

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3b1ee5cf6634798224e7816d79f73db2a6d3efddd41d718e917f3b3638c46286.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 300 + 500 = 800 m

⇒ Relative Speed (v + v) = 800 ÷ 90

⇒ 2v = 80/9 m/s

⇒ v = 40/9 m/s

⇒ To convert **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5:

⇒ Speed (v) = (40 ÷ 9) × (18 ÷ 5)

⇒ v = 8 × 2 = 16 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 16 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects move towards each other, their **relative speed** is the sum of their individual speeds: Vᵣₑₗ = V₁ + V₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5. To convert from **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18.

Crossing Objects with Length

When a train crosses another train or a bridge, the **total distance** covered is the sum of the lengths of both objects.

questions.question: An article is sold for 10 percent loss. The value of discount given is equal to the (2/7) of the selling price. What is the ratio of the marked price of the article to its cost price?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Assume **Selling Price (SP)** is 63 units (LCM of 7 and 9). At 10% loss, **Cost Price (CP)** = 63 ÷ 0.9 = 70 units. **Discount** = 2/7 × 63 = 18 units. **Marked Price (MP)** = SP + Discount = 63 + 18 = 81 units. Required Ratio **MP : CP** = 81 : 70. **∴ The correct answer is 81 : 70.**

questions.question: Which of the following will have selling price Rs. 3000?

options.text: Marked price = Rs. 4000 and Discount = 25 percent
Marked price = Rs. 4200 and Discount = 40 percent
Marked price = Rs. 3800 and Discount = 45 percent
Marked price = Rs. 3500 and Discount = 12 percent

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Target **Selling Price (SP)** = ₹3000

A **Discount** of 25% means the **SP** is 75% (or 3/4) of the **Marked Price (MP)**.

⇒ Check **Option 1**: 3/4 × ₹4000 = 3 × 1000 = ₹3000

Since the result matches target **SP**, this is the correct condition.

**∴ The correct answer is Marked price = ₹4000 and Discount = 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Target **Selling Price (SP)** = ₹3000

**Formula Used:**

**Selling Price (SP)** = **Marked Price (MP)** − **Discount**

**Discount** = (**Discount%** ÷ 100) × **Marked Price (MP)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/350d0042052828a6a42174574ce8df8de9bbbbb2bb21449ae6282619869a75a0.png] 

**Calculations:**

Evaluating **Option 1**:

⇒ **Marked Price** = ₹4000

⇒ **Discount** = 25% of ₹4000 = (25 ÷ 100) × 4000 = ₹1000

⇒ **Selling Price** = 4000 − 1000 = ₹3000 (Matches target)

Evaluating other options for verification:

⇒ **Option 2**: SP = 4200 × 0.60 = ₹2520

⇒ **Option 3**: SP = 3800 × 0.55 = ₹2090

⇒ **Option 4**: SP = 3500 × 0.88 = ₹3080

**∴ The correct answer is Marked price = ₹4000 and Discount = 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between MP, CP and Profit

The ratio of **Marked Price** to **Cost Price** is given by: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of x% and y% are applied, the **Equivalent Single Discount** = [x + y − (x × y ÷ 100)]%.

Discount Percentage Formula

**Discount%** = (**Marked Price** − **Selling Price**) ÷ **Marked Price** × 100.

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 30 percent more than its cost price. If the profit earned is 10 percent, then what is the discount offered on the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Cost Price (CP)** be 100 units.

**Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 30% of 100 = 130 units.

**Selling Price (SP)** = 100 + 10% **Profit** = 110 units.

**Discount** offered = **MP** − **SP** = 130 − 110 = 20 units.

**Discount %** = (20 ÷ 130) × 100 = 200/13 %.

**∴ The correct answer is (200/13) percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Markup Percentage** = 30%

**Profit Percentage** = 10%

**Formula Used:**

1. **Selling Price (SP)** = **Cost Price (CP)** + **Profit**

2. **Discount** = **Marked Price (MP)** − **Selling Price (SP)**

3. **Discount %** = (**Discount** ÷ **MP**) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/43df79894d0e9599872b318a3e426f2ab8227072cfeb14a0250390903aeb4671.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of the article be 100.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + (30% of 100) = 130.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 100 + (10% profit of 100) = 110.

⇒ **Discount Amount** = **MP** − **SP** = 130 − 110 = 20.

⇒ **Discount Percentage** = (**Discount Amount** ÷ **Marked Price**) × 100.

⇒ **Discount Percentage** = (20 ÷ 130) × 100 = 200/13 %.

**∴ The correct answer is (200/13) percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between CP, MP, Profit and Discount

The direct ratio formula is: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit %) ÷ (100 − Discount %). This is very useful when any three values are known.

Successive Percentage Method

Profit % = Markup % − Discount % − (Markup % × Discount %) ÷ 100. This treats the markup and discount as successive changes to the CP.

Markup Definition

Markup is the extra price added to the **Cost Price** to reach the **Marked Price**, expressed as Markup % = ((MP − CP) ÷ CP) × 100.

questions.question: 3.6, 1.2, x and 15 are in proportion. What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of the first two terms = 3.6 : 1.2 = **3 : 1**.

Since the numbers are in **proportion**, the ratio of the last two terms must also be **3 : 1**.

x : 15 = 3 : 1 ⇒ x = 15 × 3 = 45.

**∴ The correct answer is 45.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 3.6, 1.2, x, and 15 are in **proportion**.

**Formula Used:** If a, b, c, and d are in proportion, then a ÷ b = c ÷ d (or Product of Extremes = Product of Means).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d0976118c2da09e22ffb0c5636abee8810c2dfdda7337566306343f912295be.png] 

According to the **proportionality rule**:

⇒ 3.6 ÷ 1.2 = x ÷ 15

⇒ 3 = x ÷ 15

⇒ x = 3 × 15

⇒ x = 45

**∴ The correct answer is 45.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Proportion Rule

Four numbers a, b, c, d are in **proportion** if a : b = c : d, which implies ad = bc.

Mean Proportional

The **mean proportional** between two numbers a and b is given by √(a × b).

Third Proportional

If a, b, and c are in **continued proportion** (a : b = b : c), then the third proportional c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

In the proportion a : b = c : d, d is called the **fourth proportional** and is calculated as (b × c) ÷ a.

questions.question: Which of the following number should be subtracted from the 25, 15, 49 and 27 so that the remaining numbers are in proportion?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Test the **options** to find the number that makes the **ratios equal**.

Testing **Option (2)**: Subtract **5** from each number.

New numbers: (25 − 5) = 20; (15 − 5) = 10; (49 − 5) = 44; (27 − 5) = 22.

Ratio 1: 20 ÷ 10 = 2; Ratio 2: 44 ÷ 22 = 2.

Since both **ratios are equal**, the numbers are in **proportion**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given**: The numbers are **25, 15, 49, and 27**.

**Formula Used**: For four numbers a, b, c, and d to be in **proportion** after subtracting x, (a − x) ÷ (b − x) = (c − x) ÷ (d − x).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aeffcf5865902f2e7301205d5decb19f38c856624c09513665db928960db7219.png] 

**Calculations**:

⇒ (25 − x) ÷ (15 − x) = (49 − x) ÷ (27 − x)

⇒ (25 − x)(27 − x) = (15 − x)(49 − x)

⇒ 675 − 25x − 27x + x² = 735 − 15x − 49x + x²

⇒ 675 − 52x = 735 − 64x

⇒ 64x − 52x = 735 − 675

⇒ 12x = 60

⇒ x = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Proportion Shortcut Formula

For numbers a, b, c, d to be in proportion, the value to be subtracted/added is x = |(ad − bc) ÷ ((a + d) − (b + c))|.

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is calculated as √(a × b).

Continued Proportion

Three numbers a, b, and c are in continued proportion if a ÷ b = b ÷ c, which means b² = ac.
